newsitem.title: USA: Milwaukee Cty, Wis., board debates transport study.
newsitem.headline: Milwaukee Cty, Wis., board debates transport study.

text.p: The Milwaukee County Board voted Thursday to support further state study of an estimated $1.76 billion long-range transportation plan to rebuild a main East-West freeway and add light rail transit.
The board members gave their blessing to additional study 18-6 after debating the proposal Thursday afternoon, chief county board clerk Lauri Henning said.

The proposed addition of a light rail system to connect downtown Milwaukee with an adjacent county to the west has met heavy opposition. Another part of the plan that would require widening of the freeway for express lanes dedicated to public transportation and car pools has also met opposition from residents.
The plan also calls for reconstruction of two large and heavily traveled interchanges and expanded bus services that would require the purchase of new buses and construction of new facilities.
The light rail cost has been placed at about $330 million for initial construction, funded 80 percent by the federal government and 20 percent from non-federal sources.
The new bus purchases and facility improvements would cost about $90 million, according to preliminary estimates.
The interchange reconstructions have been estimated to cost $1.32 billion.
Waukesha County officials declined to give their approval of further study earlier this week.
The Wisconsin Department of Transportation must complete an environmental impact statement on the proposal and further studies must be conducted.
